What would you automate first?

Clawdbot use case: I needed to analyze 50 customer feedback emails.

Instead of reading each one:
→ Clawdbot extracted key themes
→ Summarized top complaints
→ Suggested 3 action items
→ Time saved: 2 hours

AI is not just for big companies.

Real talk: Most AI 'productivity hacks' are just faster typing.

The real wins come from:
→ Delegating entire workflows
→ Building feedback loops
→ Letting AI make suggestions you approve

Clawdbot does the second one. That's the difference.

SMB owners: You do not need an AI strategy.

You need ONE task automated this week.

Pick something that:
• Takes 30+ minutes
• Happens weekly
• Follows a pattern

That is your starting point. Everything else is noise.

Clawdbot feature spotlight: Memory that persists.

Unlike ChatGPT, Clawdbot remembers:
→ Your preferences
→ Past conversations
→ Project context
→ Your writing style

It gets smarter the more you use it.

Question for SMB owners:

What is the one task in your business that eats up time but does not require your specific expertise?

I am building a library of AI automation playbooks and want to know what actually matters to you.

Building with AI is not about replacing humans.

It is about removing the 80% of work that is repetitive so you can focus on the 20% that requires judgment, creativity, and relationships.

That is what Clawdbot is built for.

AI Myth #2: 'You need to be technical to use AI agents'

Reality: The best AI tools are conversational.

You describe what you want.
The agent figures out how to do it.

Clawdbot works this way. No coding required.

Use case: Content calendar management

Before:
→ 3 hours planning posts
→ Manual scheduling
→ Inconsistent timing

With Clawdbot:
→ Describe your goals
→ AI generates calendar
→ Auto-schedules to Buffer/Twitter
→ Time saved: 2.5 hours/week

The businesses winning with AI right now are not the ones with the biggest models.

They are the ones with the tightest feedback loops.

Ship → Measure → Learn → Ship again

Speed of iteration beats size of model. Every time.

Clawdbot vs ChatGPT:

ChatGPT = General purpose, starts fresh every time
Clawdbot = Your personal agent, remembers everything

One is a tool.
The other is a team member.

That is the difference.

Weekend thought experiment:

If you could automate one thing in your business and never think about it again, what would it be?

No constraints. Dream big.

I will share the most interesting answers next week.

Behind the scenes: How we use Clawdbot to build TheOneGroupAI

→ Drafts Twitter threads
→ Reviews code changes
→ Summarizes customer calls
→ Generates newsletter ideas
→ Tracks project tasks

We eat our own dog food. It works.

The 3-Question AI Readiness Test:

1. Do you repeat this task weekly?
2. Does it follow a pattern you could explain?
3. Would a 10% improvement matter?

If yes to all → You are ready for AI automation

Most businesses have 5-10 tasks that pass this test.

Clawdbot use case: Email triage

Problem: 200+ emails/day, important ones buried

Solution:
→ Clawdbot scans inbox hourly
→ Flags urgent items
→ Summarizes newsletters
→ Drafts responses to common questions

Result: Inbox zero by 10am, daily.

What is your biggest blocker with AI right now?

A) Do not know where to start
B) Tried tools that did not deliver
C) Worried about cost/ROI
D) Team resistance to change

Reply A/B/C/D — I will share specific resources for each.

AI tools that stick share one trait:

They do not ask users to change their workflow.
They adapt to it.

The best automation is invisible.
It just feels like you are suddenly better at your job.

That is the Clawdbot philosophy.

Use case: Meeting prep and follow-up

Before meetings:
→ Clawdbot researches attendees
→ Summarizes past interactions
→ Suggests talking points

After meetings:
→ Auto-generates summary
→ Creates action items
→ Schedules follow-ups

Time saved: 45 min per meeting

Building an AI business while using AI to build it is... meta.

Every day I discover new edge cases.
Every day the system gets smarter.

The product IS the process.

Documenting everything so others can learn from our mistakes.

Sunday reflection:

The most surprising thing about building with AI?

It is not the technology.
It is how fast your own assumptions get challenged.

What I thought users wanted ≠ What they actually need

The AI keeps me honest.
